children: Dutch and British gas prices edged lower on Thursday morning, extending this week’s losses on expectations the losses U.S. President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered in Congressional elections this week may reduce the risk of further escalation of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was down  €1.362 at €86.72 per megawatt hour (MWh) or around $28.58 /mmBtu, by 0913 GMT, ICE data showed.
The contract has now fallen around 17% since touching a high over €104/MWh last week.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) was down 3.39 pence at 215.01 pence per therm.

“After President Donald Trump's Republican Party lost control of Congress in U.S. midterm elections, the market bet that the shift in power could accelerate the end of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran,” analysts at Engie EnergyScan said in a daily market note.

Trump acknowledged that the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran had played a role in the election results, which also raised hopes of resolution to the conflict that has choked energy supplies from the Middle East.
Analysts, however, said prices are likely to remain volatile over the next few days.
“After the near 20% loss in gas prices in the past days, the market seems to have priced in significant improvements (to supply) which yet have to materialize, LSEG gas analyst Ulrich Weber said.
Flows from Norway, which have been impacted by outages, have improved slightly with total Norgegian exports expected at 330 million cubic metres/day, up 6 mcm from the previous day, LSEG data showed.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract <> was down €0.33 at €89.83 euro a metric ton.
